👑 Most Successful Overall: Tony YokielTony owns the strongest trophy case: 3 championships, the only three-peat in league history, and a league-best 13 Victory Points. His 51.34% career win rate isn't the highest, but postseason hardware separates him from everyone else.
📈 Regular-Season Standard: Sam YoungSam leads the long-tenured group with 127 career wins, a 57.21% win rate, 24,921.64 points scored and a +1,607.40 point differential. He combines longevity with elite week-to-week performance.
🔥 Best Short-Run Pace: Reid MastersReid's 62.00% win rate and 114.04 points per game are the best marks on this table, plus a championship in only four seasons. The sample is much shorter, so the site treats him as the hottest pace rather than the all-time legacy leader.
🏆 Closest Challenger: Brian CorriganBrian has 2 championships, 98 wins and a 56.98% career win rate across 13 seasons. His combination of titles and sustained winning puts him firmly in the top historical tier.
🥈 The Almost Dynasty: Shawn SmutakShawn is second in career wins with 120 and has four runner-up finishes, but no championship. A 54.05% win rate and 24,470.28 career points show sustained contention; the missing title is the biggest gap in the résumé.
⚖️ How the Scale WorksThe Legacy Score preserves your spreadsheet's Victory Points rather than inventing a new championship formula. It simply normalizes the current 0–13 scale to 0–100, making the ranking easier to visualize while keeping your league's established valuation intact.
